newsitem.title: USA: Magellan raised equities holdings in September.
newsitem.headline: Magellan raised equities holdings in September.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said its flagship Magellan Fund raised its holdings in equities to 88.9 percent of assets at the end of September from 83.9 percent at the end of August.

According to Fidelity's monthly mutual fund guide, Magellan's stake in bonds fell to 9.8 percent of assets at the end of September, the most recent date figures are available, from 11.8 percent in August.
Holdings in cash and other assets fell to 1.2 percent from 4.2 percent.
Holdings in energy stocks rose slightly, to 13.1 percent from 13.0 percent.
Durables fell to 10.6 percent of total net assets from 11.0 percent, and technology jumped to 10.7 percent from 6.7 percent, according to the fund guide.
Magellan added Intel Corp, General Electric Co and International Business Machines Corp to its top 10 holdings at the end of September.
Dropped from the list were U.S. Treasury bonds due 2023, U.S. Treasury bonds due 2026, and Exxon Corp.
Magellan's percentage of foreign investments rose to 11.7 percent of assets at the end of September from 11.1 percent at the end of August.
Net assets invested in Magellan rose to $53.23 billion at the end of October from $53.00 billion at the end of September.

During the first 10 months of the year, Magellan had a total return of 7.00 percent, compared to 16.63 percent for the S&P 500. As of October 24, Magellan had a one-year ranking from Lipper Analytical Services of 590 out of 628 growth funds.
